body:
The inability to switch back to Nest after trying Google Home feels misleading and has significantly damaged my trust in Google products. We strongly dislike the new platform. It does not provide the same level of visibility and ease of monitoring for our cameras that we previously had with Nest. As a result, we are extremely dissatisfied with this change and are now planning to replace our cameras with products from another brand.

author: Lujav
title: Nest hello
body:
I have three Nest Hello doorbell cameras, along with 18 other cameras on my property. Recently, I’ve been having constant problems with the Nest cameras. Two of them went offline for several weeks. I was eventually able to get one back online, but the other still won’t stay connected. It connects for a few moments, then disconnects again. The remaining two also keep connecting and disconnecting over and over.

The most frustrating part is that there’s no way to get ahold of anyone at Google Nest for support. It feels impossible to reach a real person, and getting help has become incredibly difficult.

I honestly wish Google had never acquired Nest. Nest was a great company with great products and excellent customer support. Since Google took over, they’ve made everything more complicated. They even discontinued the Nest app for the Apple Watch, so I can no longer control my thermostat from my watch. Their explanation was that not enough people were using it, but decisions like that have only made the user experience worse.

It feels like Google has slowly dismantled what made Nest such a great ecosystem. I really wish Nest had remained an independent company.

Pretty helpful app that lets you control your home’s thermostat right from your phone. However, the settings for creating and modifying a schedule are unnecessarily complicated and could definitely be more user-friendly.

It also seems to have a hobby of randomly putting the thermostat into “Eco Mode” and adjusting the temperature at the most inopportune times. Thankfully, having the app means you can at least change the temperature back once you notice it. 

Overall, useful app, but there’s definitely room for improvement when it comes to scheduling and Eco Mode.

body: Poor. I want a boiler controller which does as it is told what to do. What I want to avoid is the controller taking away power from the owner. body: Nest manipulates the temperature display so that you use your HVAC the way Google decides best. The actual temperature being picked up by the nest thermocouple is not revealed to the user. You can witness these effects by toggling different modes. For instance, Nest will display a current temp of 74 when set to heat at 73. But in the next instant, if you now switch to the cooling mode, it will display a current temp of 69 when set to cooling at 72. This defies physics. Bad programming.

author: Eric Otto
body: The app is great when it works. However, if your HVAC system has an issue, the app will only display "ERROR" and doesn't allow you to change the mode, so the furnace fan short cycles until the issue is fixed. The workaround to this issue is to restart your thermostat, then before it recognizes the error, set the mode to off. I'm glad I discovered this, but when in an ERROR state, the app should at least allow you to change the mode to off.
